newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls on Taiwan to avoid harming unity.
newsitem.headline: China calls on Taiwan to avoid harming unity.

text.p: China called on Taiwan on Thursday to avoid harming reunification and ethnic unity during a visit to the island by Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama.

"Taiwan authorities should see the situation clearly and not do things that will harm reunification of the country and ethnic unity," Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told reporters in response to a question on plans by Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui to meet the exiled Tibetan leader.
The Dalai Lama, who won the Nobel Peace prize in 1989 for his peaceful campaign to win greater autonomy for his Himalayan homeland, plans a six-day visit to Taiwan later this month.
China accuses him of mixing politics with religious activities in a bid to gain independence for Tibet.
"We are opposed to any person engaging in activities of any form aimed at splitting the motherland," Cui said.
"Everyone knows what kind of person the Dalai Lama is," he said. "It is also obvious what his political motives are in going to Taiwan."
